t: No contemporary source gives reliable troop counts. Jan Długosz gave the number of banners: 51 Teutonic, 50 Polish and 40 Lithuanian, but it is unclear how many men were under each.

The Lithuanian light cavalry retreated after more than an hour of fighting. Długosz called it a complete annihilation of the Lithuanian army, while some historians propose a planned feigned retreat, and Stephen Turnbull argues that it did not quite fit that pattern.

The Order held out at Marienburg and lost little land at the Peace of Thorn, yet the indemnity it had to pay brought borrowing, higher taxes and unrest in its cities, and the Poles and Lithuanians were unable to turn the military victory into territorial gains.
dyk: The site of the battle was long placed in the wrong spot. Excavations between 2014 and 2019 found the main battlefield about 2 kilometres south-west of the memorial, and the mass graves found by the old chapel probably lie near the Teutonic camp.
ev: Jogaila of Lithuania agrees in the Union of Kreva to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland, becomes Władysław II Jagiełło and creates a personal union of Poland and Lithuania
An uprising in Samogitia leads the Teutonic Order to declare war on Poland and Lithuania, and it invades Greater Poland and Kuyavia
A truce is signed in October, due to expire on 24 June 1410, and both sides prepare for war
The Polish and Lithuanian armies unite at Czerwińsk, cross the Vistula and enter Prussia in early July
The two armies fight between Grünfelde, Tannenberg and Ludwigsdorf, and Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen is killed
The main Polish and Lithuanian forces reach Marienburg in late July, and the siege is lifted on 19 September
Władysław II Jagiełło defeats the Order again in the Battle of Koronowo in October
The Peace of Thorn returns Dobrin Land to Poland, and the Order resigns its claims to Samogitia for the lifetimes of Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas

f.place: Between the villages of Grünfelde (Grunwald), Tannenberg (Stębark) and Ludwigsdorf (Łodwigowo) in the Teutonic Order's territory, in present-day Poland; excavations of 2014 to 2019 placed the main battlefield about 2 kilometres south-west of the traditional site, south of Grunwald
f.sides: The Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas, against the Teutonic Order under Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen; the contemporary sources give no reliable troop counts, and the high-end estimates of Stefan Kuczyński, 39,000 Polish and Lithuanian and 27,000 Teutonic men, are often cited in Western literature as commonly accepted
f.outcome: The Teutonic army was defeated and Grand Master von Jungingen was killed, with much of the Order's leadership. The Order held out at Marienburg and lost little land in the Peace of Thorn of 1411, but it never recovered its former power.
